case.court_name: Court of Appeal of Sri Lanka
case.source_citation: CA 169/2003, High Court Gampaha 48/94, decided 16 June 2008

clause.text: Any accused person has the right to a fair trial and legal representation.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the failure to read out the charge and record a plea at the retrial violated the accused's right to a fair trial under Article 13(3).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The accused-appellant argued that the indictment and charge were not read out and no plea was recorded at the second trial, violating his right to a fair trial.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Attorney-General contended that this was a procedural irregularity without prejudice since the accused was already familiar with the charge from the first trial.
key_facts: The accused was retried after an appeal ordered a retrial.
At the retrial, the indictment and charge were not read out and no plea was recorded.
The first trial had complied with these procedural requirements.
The accused was not served with the indictment before the retrial.
The trial judge failed to amend the indictment to delete the acquitted co-accused's name.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(3) guarantees the accused a fair trial according to procedure established by law, which includes reading the charge and recording a plea at the start of trial. This procedural step is mandatory and not merely directory.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the retrial was a distinct trial, the failure to read the charge and record a plea at the retrial violated the accused's right to a fair trial under Article 13(3). The accused was handicapped in preparing his defense and instructing counsel.
principles_established: A retrial is a separate trial requiring full compliance with procedural safeguards.
Failure to read the charge and record a plea is a fundamental defect, not a mere technical irregularity.
Article 13(3) protects the right to a fair trial including procedural fairness.

outcome.holding: The appeal was allowed on this ground, the conviction and sentence were set aside, and the accused was acquitted.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Conviction for murder under Section 296 and death penalty set aside; accused acquitted.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(3) was central to the court's reasoning that the accused's right to a fair trial was violated by the failure to read the charge and record a plea at the retrial, leading to the setting aside of the conviction.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court stated it is a fundamental right of an accused to a fair trial in accordance with procedure established by law under Article 13(3). The failure to read the charge and record a plea at the retrial was unfair and unreasonable, handicapping the accused's defense.
